# Explain archive identity and source prerequisites before installation

During the real city reuse test, the model copied inner pet/weather resource
hashes into catalog AssetRefs. The archive identity guard correctly rejected
them. After correcting those refs, the older pet component failed its fixed
legacy adapter requirement in a controller-v1 world. The approved Pomeranian
version declared an exact matching profile and subsequently installed.

Add explicit install/read references and advisory source prerequisite metadata
to existing read responses. Reuse the composition requirement assessment rule,
preserve source pins and report mismatches before an attempted write. Keep
search pagination/ranking and every installation guard unchanged. Do not infer
runtime compatibility from a source match or substitute an unlisted package.

This is additive model response metadata, not a new installation path or a
relaxation of hashes, permissions, profiles, source ownership or gameplay checks.

## Amendment: automatic instance declarations (2026-09-15)

The real monster-creation turn repeatedly encountered combat v1's three declared
entity IDs with only one `sceneInstall`. The installer correctly required one
entity per automatic scene instance. Neither placement changes nor a fabricated
entity-selection parameter could repair that immutable archive. Its GDScripts
also lacked the UID files required by source installation.

Extend the existing advisory response contract with `automaticInstallation` on
read results and under search results' `targetCompatibility`. An intrinsic
declaration failure is `installation-declaration-blocked`; receiving-source
assessment remains separate in `sourcePrerequisitesStatus`. Inspect returned
archives even if source assessment is unavailable, because malformed package
declarations do not depend on a receiving world. Keep original search order,
pagination, error codes and exact catalog references.

Explain the supported recovery rather than implying that different parameters
will fix the package. Combat v1 remains unchanged. Version 2 declares its actual
single automatic monster and includes deterministic script UIDs. Its
machine-readable `installationGuide` distinguishes bundled scripts from automatic
nodes: pursuit and player damage require a separately mounted, unique player
vitals component, and weapon setup remains optional work for the player's later
request. Normal project read/edit, source CAS, checks and adoption remain the
only mutation path; the metadata grants no authority or ready-gameplay status.

The CPU regression proves unchanged v1 refusal and successful v2 source
installation with two independent monster identities and all helper files.
It does not prove v2 combat gameplay. The subsequent real-model continuation
selected ordinary source authoring instead of v2, so it supplies no v2 gameplay
acceptance evidence. See the [response contract](../spec/source-library-reference-hints.md)
and [focused validation scenario](../e2e/combat-install-contract-20260915.md).

### Retained proposal projection

Old proposal cards otherwise continue to advertise installation or generic
conversation retry after an immutable declaration failure is known. Extend the
same advisory metadata into their read projection, verified against each frozen
archive identity. Do not migrate stored proposal status or infer a current-task
failure from an old attempt. Existing job evidence wins; unreadable or changed
archives remain unknown. This additive response controls only the known-invalid
UI affordance, while unchanged native installation guards remain authoritative.

Apply that same intrinsic check to the existing direct-inspection response so
opening the original bad version in the library does not re-enable the failed
installation route. Reuse `eligible` and `reason`, with no new RPC or alternate
installation path. Unknown/read-failure cases retain their earlier behavior;
only a hash-verified, known declaration mismatch receives the new unavailable
message. Selection and upgrade remain explicit player actions.
